findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the parity_report reference enumeration to include parallel_run_and_diff (parity.py:302) and fidelity_spot_eval.py:194, while keeping the (correct) conclusion that none is a production gate caller.

search_files: src/rebar/llm/parity.py:302 `return parity_report(v1, v2)` inside `parallel_run_and_diff`; src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py:194 `return parity.parity_report(v1, v2, min_gold=SPOT_MIN_GOLD)`

The load-bearing conclusion ('ZERO production callers') is unaffected: parallel_run_and_diff is a live driver in parity.py and fidelity_spot_eval is an opt-in operator eval, neither a production gate caller.
findings.finding: The plan states that under `src/` the only references to `parity_report` are 'its own definition and two internal reuses, container_fidelity_report and prerequisite_fidelity_report' — but two further callers exist: parity.parallel_run_and_diff (parity.py:302) and fidelity_spot_eval.py:194 (parity.parity_report directly).
findings.location: Approach → 'Correcting an earlier claim in this plan'
scenarios: A reader auditing the parity_report call graph to confirm 'zero production callers' finds the plan's enumeration understates the actual reference set.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to: 'under `src/` the references are its own definition, two internal reuses (container_fidelity_report, prerequisite_fidelity_report), the parallel_run_and_diff live driver, and the opt-in fidelity_spot_eval — none of them a production gate caller.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the `decision` value an errored `ItemRecord` carries and how the harness prevents errored gold pairs from being counted in `parity_report`'s `decision_flips` (e.g. exclude `errored` items from the paired flip count or drop them before `parity_report`), so a transient runtime error marks the slot INVALID rather than registering as a decision flip.
evidence: Plan: 'An epoch that raises is recorded as an errored `ItemRecord` … distinct from `decision_flips`' and 'feeds the averaged paired `ItemRecord` lists straight to `parity_report`'
parity.py:107 `decision_flips = sum(1 for a, b in gold_pairs if a.decision != b.decision)` — no `errored` guard; every gold pair with mismatched decision counts, including errored ones
fidelity_spot_eval.py:174 the precedent gives an all-errored item `decision="dropped"` with `label=<gold>`, which `dropped != block/advisory` would count as a flip
parity.py:32 `_DECISIONS = ("block", "advisory", "dropped")` — 'dropped' is a real decision, so an errored 'dropped' record is not skipped by the label filter
findings.finding: The plan says errored ItemRecords are counted 'distinct from decision_flips', but it never pins the `decision` value an errored ItemRecord carries, and parity_report counts decision_flips over ALL gold pairs with no errored exclusion — so an errored v2 record (decision='dropped' per the precedent) paired against a block/advisory v1 record will silently register as a decision-level flip, contradicting the plan's own error-classification invariant and potentially failing a slot for a transient runtime error rather than marking it INVALID.
findings.location: Approach → 'Error classification' and 'Repeats'; scored against src/rebar/llm/parity.py:104-107 and fidelity_spot_eval.py:174
scenarios: A single transient throttle/500 on one v2 gold item (not a temperature/auth error) yields decision='dropped' and registers as '1 decision-level flip(s) on the gold set (must be 0)', failing the slot as a Bedrock non-inferiority failure rather than a re-runnable INVALID.
findings.suggested_fix: State that errored items are filtered out of the paired lists fed to `parity_report` (recorded only in the classifier's own error-count fields), OR add an `errored`-exclusion to the flip computation, and give the errored `ItemRecord` a documented sentinel decision that the harness never pairs into the gold flip count.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the error-classifier discrimination rule: capture the raised exception string, and state the precedence (match 'temperature' in the message FIRST → sampling-parameter bucket, then AccessDeniedException/ValidationException → auth/validation bucket, else generic errored), rather than reusing the precedent's exception-discarding `except Exception`.
evidence: Plan: 'A sampling-parameter rejection (a 400 naming `temperature`) and an authorization / validation refusal are counted and reported in their own fields'

iam_s7.tf:26-28 records `AccessDeniedException` on InvokeModel and the plan's Step-1 example uses `ValidationException: … on-demand throughput isn't supported` — both are 400-class, and a temperature rejection is also a ValidationException, so 'naming temperature' must be checked FIRST or it is swept into the generic validation bucket
fidelity_spot_eval.py:170 the copied `_record` uses `except Exception:` and appends '__error__', discarding the exception — so the classifier as-shaped cannot see the error string it must key on
findings.finding: The net-new error classifier's discrimination rule is under-specified: it must sort a sampling-parameter rejection (400 naming `temperature`), an auth refusal (AccessDeniedException) and a validation refusal (ValidationException) — but temperature rejections are THEMSELVES ValidationExceptions, and the plan neither states the classification precedence (temperature-check before the generic validation bucket) nor that the raised exception object/string must be captured for classification, while the precedent it copies (`_record`) discards the exception via a bare `except Exception`.
findings.location: Approach → 'Error classification' and 'Step 1'; scored against fidelity_spot_eval.py:170 and bedrock error shapes in iam_s7.tf:26-28
scenarios: A temperature-400 (a ValidationException) is classified as a generic validation refusal because the precedence is unstated, or the exception string is discarded before the classifier runs, so a configuration defect is silently recorded as an authorization/validation finding instead of the temperature-capability fix the plan mandates.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that each epoch's exception is captured (not swallowed) and classified by an ordered predicate: (1) message contains 'temperature' → sampling-parameter rejection; (2) AccessDeniedException / ValidationException → auth/validation refusal; (3) otherwise → generic errored — with counts kept in separate result fields.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the provider-clean tally technique to read the JSONL usage log as JSON objects (e.g. filter rows where `"model"` and `"input_tokens"` keys are present, or reuse `rebar.llm.usage_log`'s own reader) instead of grepping for `model=`/`input_tokens=` shell-style tokens.
evidence: Plan: 'Extract per-call model only from log lines carrying BOTH `model=` and `input_tokens=`; a whole-log grep for the model id over-counts'

usage_log.py writes rows via `json.dumps(row)` with keys `row["model"]`, and `_FIELDS = ("input_tokens", ...)` written as `row[field]` (usage_log.py:298-315, :32) — JSON object keys, not `model=`/`input_tokens=` pairs
prompt-eval.yml:83 names the file `usage.jsonl` and its comment says 'one JSONL line per LLM call'
REBAR_USAGE_LOG is the rig the plan cites at prompt-eval.yml:83,110-112, which summarizes via `python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize` — a JSON reader, not a grep
findings.finding: The provider-clean verification technique (extract per-call model from REBAR_USAGE_LOG lines 'carrying BOTH model= and input_tokens=', via a 'whole-log grep for the model id') describes a key=value shell-line shape, but the actual usage log is JSONL — one JSON object per line with keys "model" and "input_tokens", not model=/input_tokens= tokens. A grep for model=/input_tokens= will match nothing, defeating the v2-arm-provider-clean proof as written.
findings.location: Testing → 'Live, opt-in' step 2, and the '[operator-attested] The v2 arm is proven provider-clean' AC
scenarios: Operator runs the live paired run, then greps the usage log for `model=` to build the per-call tally and gets zero matches, unable to prove the v2 arm made zero non-Bedrock calls
findings.suggested_fix: State the extraction as: parse each JSONL row as a JSON object, keep rows with both a `model` field and a non-null `input_tokens` field, and tally by `model` (or `provider`) — mirroring how `rebar.llm.usage_log.summarize` consumes the same file — rather than a substring grep for `model=`.

evidence: Subject: 'The gate's per-pass model ladder is likewise not in play: RunRequest carries no model-class field, so a single-prompt eval case resolves cfg.model and nothing else. That is why this harness — rather than a paired rebar review-plan run — is the right instrument.'

Prerequisite 3768: '0d76 (parity bar) compares v1=Anthropic against v2=Bedrock. Without per-pass control the arms differ in TWO variables (provider AND per-pass model class), so any criterion failure is unattributable and any pass is unrepresentative of production.'
findings.finding: The subject plan deliberately runs both arms through a single-prompt eval path where each case resolves only `cfg.model` and nothing else. It states the gate's per-pass model ladder is 'not in play' because `RunRequest` carries no model-class field, and treats this as the reason the harness rather than a paired `rebar review-plan` run is the right instrument. But prerequisite 3768's central deliverable is per-pass model class resolution (opus-family Pass-1, sonnet-family Pass-2/Pass-4) so that a Bedrock parity comparison does not differ in two variables. Prerequisite 3768 explicitly names 0d76 (the parity bar) as a story it blocks precisely so the arms differ in only one variable — yet the subject plan achieves single-variable comparison by collapsing to a single-prompt path that exercises NO per-pass class distinction at all. The subject measures each class slot in isolation with a single flat model per arm, not the multi-pass per-class resolution that 3768 exists to make attributable and representative of production. The subject's claim that the ladder is irrelevant to its instrument is in tension with 3768's stated purpose that per-pass control is what makes the parity comparison representative.
